paragraphs.text: The three paragraph measures of The Federalist No. 10, to see where the essay is harder going and where it eases.
Each measure over the essay's 23 paragraphs, one panel each:

Each paragraph carries readability_grade, lexical_density and compression_ratio in its metrics. The document's own metrics, beside its sections, carry the counts, the sentence-length statistics, vocabulary_ttr, nominalization_ratio and passive_ratio.

The grade runs from 10.69 (paragraph 3) to 32.06 (paragraph 18). It is the Flesch-Kincaid formula over sentence length and syllables per word (Methodology), so an eighteenth-century paragraph of a few long sentences scores far above any school grade. Compare paragraphs with each other, not with a grade band.
compression_ratio is null for four paragraphs, the ones of 50 words or fewer. null means the measure declined to run, not that it measured zero; which measure needs what is in the Rust guide.
